fields.features_heading: Inside a Hair Type Quiz Built on Emergent
fields.features_subheading: A hair type quiz sorts answers on how hair dries and curls into one hair type. Emergent builds the quiz and the data behind it.
fields.feature_1:
Every option tied to one result

Name the results, such as Wavy or Coily, and say what sets each one apart. Emergent writes the questions, and every option counts toward one result. Reword any of them by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
A routine on each result screen

Tag the cleanser, leave-in, and styler that suit each hair type in the app's product table. The result screen lists those products, and a product you retag appears on the next quiz.
fields.feature_3:
Each finished quiz saved as a row

The result, every option picked, and an email when one is given land as one row in a database you own. Filter by Coily to see how often those visitors said they wash their hair.
fields.feature_4:
One question per screen on a phone

Emergent builds the quiz as a conversational flow, one question per screen and sized for a phone. A visitor arriving from a social post can finish all eight with one thumb.
fields.feature_5:
An alert when a result needs a stylist

Send a Slack or email alert when a result needs a person, such as a Coily result on a salon booking. The stylist gets the client's name and result next to the appointment time.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain now, your code on paid plans

Put the quiz on your shop's domain: custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. Paid plans add full code export to your GitHub repository for your developer.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Hair Type Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a hair type quiz that puts each visitor in one result and gives them a routine that fits it.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask how hair looks after it air-dries
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Put a routine in every result
fields.howto_step_1_des: Settle the results before writing a question. Straight, wavy, curly, and coily are the four main hair types. Add the letter subtypes only if your products or services change between them, because twelve results need more questions to tell apart.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open with how hair looks after a wash and an air-dry with no product, which is how stylists read a type. Then ask about oil at the roots and how often it needs a wash. Each question should separate the results, not repeat one.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write one option per result for every question, in words a shopper recognizes: loose S-shaped bends, not a subtype code. Keep the four options close in length, so the longest one never looks like the right answer.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Every result should say what to do next. Name a cleanser, a leave-in, and a styler for that hair type, or the service a salon books for it. A result that only names the type leaves the visitor where they began.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Ask for an email after the result
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide what to keep with each result: the options picked, plus an email only when the visitor offers one. Put the email field after the result screen, never before it. Say in one line what you will send to that address.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it on four heads of hair
fields.howto_step_6_des: Have four people you know take the quiz, one for each result, and check that each lands where you expect. When two results tie for someone, reword the question that separated them least and run the test again.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the counts after a month
fields.howto_step_7_des: After a month, compare the count for each hair type and the answers behind it. Replace any question every visitor answers the same way. If one result leads by a wide margin, check that your shelf or service menu matches it.

faq_plan.q: What is a hair type quiz?
faq_plan.a: A hair type quiz is a short set of questions about how your hair dries and curls, scored into one hair type. Hair comes in four main types: straight, wavy, curly, and coily. The quiz on this page uses those four and ends each result with a care routine.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a hair type quiz?
faq_plan.a: Describe the results and the business behind them, and Emergent's AI survey builder writes the questions and the table that stores each result. Ask for a product list or an email field on the result screen with a follow-up prompt, then publish the quiz link.

faq_plan.q: Should a curly hair type quiz split Curly into letter subtypes?
faq_plan.a: Only if your advice changes between them. The four types are broken down into subtypes A, B, and C based on texture, thickness, and curl pattern. If a 3A and a 3C visitor would get the same products, keep one Curly result and add a follow-up question on curl size.

faq_plan.q: Can I offer a hair type quiz free to every visitor on my site?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Charge nothing to take it, and use the result to point visitors to products or a booking. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing the quiz. A brand that also sells clothing can run a style quiz on the same site.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a hair types quiz have?
faq_plan.a: Eight questions are enough to separate four results. Give each question one screen and one option per result. Stop at ten, and cut any question whose answers never change a result.

faq_plan.q: How does a what's my hair type quiz decide the result?
faq_plan.a: It counts answers. Each option points to one result, and the result with the most points wins. In the quiz above, a tie goes to the result listed first. On Emergent, every answer sits beside its result in a database you own, so you can see which question decided a close call.

faq_plan.q: Does a hair type quiz for female customers need different questions?
faq_plan.a: No. The questions are about the hair itself: how it dries and holds a curl. Ask about length or styling habits only if your results change with them. Write every option in plain words, because the quiz should never read like a vocabulary quiz on terms such as porosity.

faq_plan.q: Can a quiz for hair type recommend products from my store?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Tag each product with the hair types it suits, and the app lists the matching ones on each result screen. If your catalog lives on another store platform, an app built on Emergent can connect to it through its API and read the tags from there.

faq_plan.q: Should a hair type quiz ask about porosity?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if your products differ by it. Porosity refers to how much moisture your hair absorbs and holds. Ask about it as something the visitor can see at home, show it as a separate line on the result, and test the wording on a few people before it changes any recommendation.

faq_plan.q: How do I get more people to take my hair type quiz?
faq_plan.a: Put the quiz where hair decisions happen: on product pages, in the order confirmation, and on the booking page. If you sell a trial-size kit, send each result to a free trial landing page for that kit. Link the quiz from posts that show the four hair types side by side.

quiz.title: What Is Your Hair Type?
quiz.intro: Eight questions about how your hair dries and holds a curl. Your result names the hair type your answers lean toward, with a routine to start from.

questions.text: Wash your hair and let it air-dry with no product. How does it look?

options.text: Straight, with no wave or curl
A slight curve or soft S shape
Coiled curls that spiral
Tight, well-defined coils

source.quote: To learn your hair type, wash and then air dry it.

questions.text: Look closely at one dry curl. What shape does it make?

options.text: There is no curl to look at
A loose S
A spiral or tight corkscrew
A Z with sharp-angled bends

source.quote: look like a "Z" with a sharp-angled zigzag pattern where the hair bends

questions.text: How would you describe your hair overall?

options.text: Smooth, with a natural shine
Fairly straight, with a soft bend
Defined curls that tend to feel dry
Dense and coarse-looking, but fragile

source.quote: it's actually made up of many fine hairs tightly packed together, which makes it more fragile than straighter hair.

questions.text: A day after washing, how do your roots and ends feel?

options.text: Oily at the roots already
Neither oily nor dry
Fine at the roots, dry toward the ends
Dry from root to tip

source.quote: It tends to be drier because oil has a harder time reaching the bottom of a curled hair shaft.

questions.text: Without heat tools, does your hair hold a wave or curl?

options.text: No, it only curls with heat styling and products
A soft wave, and it curls with a styling product
Yes, curls that stay in place once styled
Yes, tight coils with no help at all

source.quote: It doesn't curl or wave unless you use heat styling and products on it.

questions.text: Which product does your hair ask for most?

options.text: A lightweight conditioner that won't weigh it down
Light hydrating products and a leave-in
A mousse or curl-defining cream
A hydrating conditioner that holds in moisture

source.quote: Use a mousse or curl-defining cream to give hair structure without weighing it down.

questions.text: How often does your hair need a wash?

options.text: About every other day, with a volumizing shampoo
About every third day
Once a week at most, then a deep conditioner
Every two to three days, with a mild shampoo

source.quote: Limit washing to once a week to prevent your hair from drying out.

questions.text: Which haircut advice fits your hair best?

options.text: Face-framing layers to give it movement
Long, soft layers broken up by a few shorter ones
Layers on the sides and top to lighten the curls
Internal layers to give it more shape

source.quote: Huacuja suggests adding some layers along the sides and on top to lighten it up.

results.title: Straight
results.description: Your answers lean toward straight hair: it dries straight, with no wave or curl. Wash about every other day with a volumizing shampoo, then use a lightweight conditioner that won't weigh it down.

results.title: Wavy
results.description: Your answers lean toward wavy hair: a slight curve or soft S shape. Wash about every third day, use light hydrating products and a leave-in conditioner, then style with a gel made to control frizz.

results.title: Curly
results.description: Your answers lean toward curly hair: coiled curls, from loose curls to tight corkscrews. Wash once a week at most, follow with a deep conditioning treatment, and give curls structure with a mousse or curl-defining cream.

results.title: Coily
results.description: Your answers lean toward coily hair: tight, well-defined coils. Wash every two to three days with a mild shampoo, work a leave-in conditioner through with your fingers or a comb, and brush gently to avoid breakage.

findings.field: quiz results, quiz questions Q3-Q6, howto_step_2_des
findings.quote: Your answers lean toward wavy hair: loose S-shaped bends that start below the ears.
findings.issue: The quiz and how-to state traits of each hair type as fact, but domain_sources holds only the four types, the A/B/C subtypes and the porosity definition. The cited WebMD page supports the S shape (type 2), spirals (3B), zigzags and shrinking as it dries (4B, not curly), oily straight hair and frizz in humidity (type 2, 3A); it says nothing on where waves or coils start, heat hiding the pattern, brushing, or creams weighing hair down. Every instance: (1) howto_step_2_des 'since heat and styling hide the pattern'; (2) result wavy 'start below the ears'; (3) result wavy 'Brushing dry hair turns waves to fluff'; (4) result curly 'springy spirals that shrink as they dry' (source gives shrinkage for type 4B); (5) result coily 'tight coils or zigzags that start at the scalp'; (6) result straight 'Skip heavy creams, which weigh straight strands down'; (7) Q5 options 'Around the ears or below -> wavy', 'Close to the roots -> curly', 'Right at the scalp -> coily'; (8) Q6 'The waves get bigger -> wavy', 'The coils draw up even tighter -> coily' (source: type 2 and 3A frizz); (9) Q3 shrinkage ladder 'A little shorter' / 'Noticeably shorter' / 'Much shorter'; (10) Q4 brushing ladder 'waves loosen into fluff' / 'curls break up into frizz' / 'coils puff into a soft cloud'.
findings.fix: Add quoted spans for each trait kept (up to 8 sources; WebMD already covers S shape, spirals, zigzags, 4B shrinkage, type 1 oil, humidity frizz), and rewrite or drop every trait no source states; keep care tips as advice ('Try a light conditioner'), not as facts with a 'which/because' reason.
